subject.title: Telegram owner commands: trusted execution mode for approval-gated actions

question: Should OpenClaw add a trusted-owner approval-bypass mode for Telegram group-origin privileged actions, and should it live as a shared execution policy instead of a Telegram-only boolean?
rationale: Source and release checks show the mode is missing, but deciding when a channel identity may skip privileged-action approvals changes a security boundary and config surface that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design shared trusted-owner policy
options.body: Add a disabled-by-default shared policy with explicit sender, allowlisted group, tool-class, destructive-operation, audit, docs, and regression-test semantics across the approval stack.

options.title: Keep current approval model
options.body: Decline a bypass and document that low-friction trusted setups should use existing exec/elevated policy with intentionally permissive host approvals.

options.title: Add Telegram-only shortcut
options.body: Implement the proposed Telegram config directly, accepting a narrower patch but higher risk of policy drift from shared approvals and elevated execution.

recommendation.title: Design shared trusted-owner policy
recommendation.body: Add a disabled-by-default shared policy with explicit sender, allowlisted group, tool-class, destructive-operation, audit, docs, and regression-test semantics across the approval stack.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans product security posture, config surface, and cross-approval ownership before Telegram implementation can proceed.
